thread:
anya (eng-platform): Heads up — noticed a spike in hosted token spend for free-tier customers yesterday. Telemetry shows a bunch of requests got routed to the high-cost model instead of the cheaper variant. Any ideas?

 tom (eng-runtime): saw that too in the traces. routing logs show fallback to `rw-largex-v2` for ~12% of short-chat requests from NA. suspiciously correlated with a per-region capacity fallback rule.

 jess (devex): ugh. that will blow cost targets. Is the fallback policy prioritizing latency over cost?

 anya (eng-platform): yeah current policy is: prefer latency SLO -> same model family -> region. cost isn't in the decision tree. we default to cheapest-compatible only when tier==free AND region==eu in prod routing table, but seems the tier match failed for some customers.

 srini (product): what's our ask? Do we want a global cost-aware policy that explicitly downgrades non-paid tiers to quantized/smaller variants, or more of an emergency fallback when capacity is low?

 charlie (eng-api): two separate problems: 1) deterministic mapping for tier->variant so customers get consistent quality, 2) clear token-budget enforcement so a single runaway customer doesn't eat free pool.

 pagerbot: [alert] 2026-03-15T14:22:07Z high token spend detected — free-tier NA cluster — +18% over baseline.

 tom (eng-runtime): proposal sketch (config snippet):

 ```yaml
 routing_policies:
   - name: cost_aware_tiering
     match:
       customer_tier: [free, trial]
     rules:
       - priority: 100
         selector: {region: NA}
         action:
           prefer_models: [rw-small-v1-quant, rw-medium-v1-quant]
           max_cost_per_1k_tokens: 0.75 # USD equivalent unit
       - priority: 90
         selector: {region: EU}
         action:
           prefer_models: [rw-medium-v1-quant, rw-small-v1-quant]
           max_cost_per_1k_tokens: 0.9
     fallback: allow_higher_cost_if_latency_violation: true
 ```

 tom (eng-runtime): idea is router checks model cost profiles and enforces cheap variants for free/trial tiers unless latency SLO would be missed.

 jess (devex): for console UX: we should show per-customer "routing policy" with preview of actual model chosen for a sample prompt. Toggle to opt-in to cost_aware routing per org + a global rollout switch.

 srini (product): +1 on preview. Also want audit logs for when a request got downgraded for cost reasons (so support can explain regressions).

 charlie (eng-api): implementation note: do we put token budget enforcement in the router (fast path) or in the accounting service (post-fact)? If in accounting service we risk reactive throttles and surprise for users. If in router we need to query per-customer budgets (higher latency).

 tom (eng-runtime): we can cache budget windows in the router with a TTL and soft quotas. quick check: if budget_remaining < threshold -> route to cheaper model. That keeps it fast. final charge still goes through billing service.

 anya (eng-platform): agree. router cache + eventual consistency seems pragmatic. let's also include a deterministic variant mapping table so clients see stable behavior across retries.

 jess (devex): for the rollout UX: expose a feature flag 'cost_aware_routing' in Console with: OFF / SAFE (only free/trial) / AGGRESSIVE (include low-tier paid too) + % rollout control. show 7d impact estimate on cost and p95 latency.

 tom (eng-runtime): test plan: A/B 5% accounts -> measure: cost_per_1k_tokens, fallback_rate (to higher-cost), p50/p95 latency, quality_regressions via existing evals on sampled prompts.

 charlie (eng-api): small snippet to simulate routing decision via internal API for testing:

 curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood.local/v1/router/simulate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"customer_id":"acct_123","tier":"free","region":"NA","seq_len":64,"prompt":"hello"}'

 response: `{ "selected_model": "rw-small-v1-quant", "reason": "cost_match, budget_cache_ok" }`

 srini (product): make sure the console shows the "simulated selection" so support/devs can repro. Also tie the rollout to existing canary infra so we can quickly rollback.

 anya (eng-platform): one open API debate: should the routing policy language allow arbitrary expressions (cost < X and latency_risk < Y) or be declarative only? expressive DSL gives power but ops complexity.

 tom (eng-runtime): prefer declarative with limited expressions. keep runtime simple. we can add a tiny expression syntax later if needed.

 jess (devex): UX concern: if we auto-downgrade models, customers will notice quality diffs. need a clear consent path and opt-out per org, plus a "last-mile" preview in the Console before enabling.

 charlie (eng-api): also add short-term telemetry: a new metric `routing.variant.swap_rate` labeled by customer_tier, region, and model_from/model_to. first few weeks we can monitor and alert if swap_rate exceeds threshold for paid tiers.

 anya (eng-platform): action items: 1) tom: prototype router budget cache + deterministic mapping (PR by EOD Wed) 2) jess: mock Console rollout + simulate UI preview by Thu 3) charlie: add simulate API + metric labels 4) srini: finalize product policy for SAFE vs AGGRESSIVE by Friday

 tom (eng-runtime): I'll push a PoC branch and add unit tests for TTL cache and policy evaluation.

 jess (devex): I'll wire a fake-preview using sample prompts so PMs can eyeball.

 srini (product): cool. let's try 5% A/B in NA for free/trial groups first. keep paid tiers out of AGGRESSIVE mode for now.

 anya (eng-platform): thanks — will post follow-ups with PR links and a short runbook for support. :thumbsup:

 charlie (eng-api): one more note: ensure audit logs include model_hash + policy_version for reproducibility.

 pagerbot: [deployment] cost-aware-routing feature flag created: feature.cost_aware_routing (state=off)

 tom (eng-runtime): nice. I'll flip to a 0.1 toggle in the staging org once PoC passes.

 jess (devex): keeping this thread for progress updates — short messages preferred.

 anya (eng-platform): yep. ping me if you hit policy edge cases.
